nodes.label: Q1: Do Haiku rules hold in live use?
nodes.explain: Does the new easy-tier rubric (Haiku only for mechanical work with a cheap check, effort low, medium on long prompts) send only safe work to Haiku in live sessions? Settled by: No argument settles it, because the rubric has not yet run in a session that loaded it. Read the first week of simple-tier rows in ~/projects/data/logs/router/*.tsv and the weekly review, then read a sample of simple-tier transcripts in full; the result changes the Haiku share rule and nothing else.

nodes.label: Tier
nodes.explain: The router's grade for a task: easy, normal, hard or long, each tied to a model (Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1). Source: README.md:17. Code: hooks/lib/pricing.ts:22.

nodes.label: Classifier verdict
nodes.explain: Haiku 5.5's reading of a task as a tier and a risk flag, cached by task key. Source: README.md:35. Code: hooks/lib/pricing.ts:396.

nodes.label: Effort cap
nodes.explain: The most reasoning effort a tier's requests may ask for; it only ever lowers effort. Easy low (medium over about 50k tokens), normal medium, hard high, long unchanged. Source: README.md:19. Code: hooks/lib/pricing.ts:53.

nodes.label: Q2: Do outcome signals miss silent errors?
nodes.explain: The outcome labels (failed tools, rescued, redone, fixer started within 30 minutes) catch loud failure; how often does a Haiku or Sonnet run give a wrong answer none of them sees? Settled by: Argument settles the direction: absence of a retry is weak evidence, and the review already says so. Sampling traces is the only way to measure the rate, so lowering proposals carry 'read these traces' and a session samples before accepting.

nodes.label: Weekly review

nodes.label: Q3: Research claims not yet re-checked
nodes.explain: The research report marks its Haiku figures (32% cost saved for about 4 points of pass rate; low effort skips checks in long prompts) as read from Anthropic pages but says load-bearing claims need a re-check; do the pages still say that? Settled by: Prior art settles it: re-read the two cited pages (optimizing-for-cost-and-intelligence, effort) and compare the numbers. No test needed.

nodes.label: Q4: Can a plugin set the main model?
nodes.explain: Can any plugin mechanism set the main conversation's model or effort? The report read only the first 100k of 288k characters of the hooks reference and says to grep the tail for setModel and CLAUDE_ENV_FILE before relying on 'impossible'. Settled by: Prior art: grep the unread tail of the hooks and model-config pages for setModel, model in hook output and CLAUDE_ENV_FILE.

nodes.label: Main-model lever
nodes.explain: The two settings that do set the main model: the model default in ~/.claude/settings.json (sonnet) and /model or /effort. Source: README.md:77. Not implemented here.

nodes.label: Main conversation
nodes.explain: The session Brian types into. A plugin cannot change its model or effort (open question Q4 checks the unread part of the docs). Source: docs/planning/research-routing-best-practices.md:55. Not implemented here.

nodes.label: Q5: Who applies a tier decision?
nodes.explain: When a session accepts a weekly decision (for example lower general-purpose from hard to standard), does it edit the tier rules directly and ship, or does a pull request wait for Brian? Recommendation: An agent session accepts or rejects each decision after reading the traces, ships the rule change through ship, and records the decision; Brian reads the weekly page only if he wants to. Default: Recommendation applies: the session that reads the weekly review decides and ships; nothing waits for Brian.

nodes.label: Q8: Fork has no LICENSE
nodes.explain: The plugin directory check refuses a submission without a LICENSE; the fork and its upstream (aott33/model-router) have none. Does that matter? Settled by: Argument settles it: the fork is installed from a marketplace entry, not submitted to the directory, and a license is the upstream author's choice, not ours. No test needed. Revisit only if Brian wants the fork listed.
